correctness.rationale: For all signed stars, the a-positive leaves must join the hub and a-negative leaves must remain outside; this leaves only the hub payoff U and the sums of outsider blocks to check. Grouping outsiders proves the necessary and sufficient U/R existence criterion and labeled-block exponential formula. Hoeffding concentration and a triangular-array CLT prove the random reciprocity threshold and Gaussian window. Joint sign inversion plus Vandermonde yields the exact odd/even critical probability. Independently enumerated all 1,365 signed profiles with up to five leaves, evaluating 222,233 direct game-partition cases and comparing the exact counting recurrence; 30 additional exact-rational parameter checks passed. These finite checks are not substitutes for the general proof.

evidence: General hard instances and upper-bound algorithms do not give a necessary-and-sufficient formula for all unit signed stars.
The 2024 random model uses independent continuous valuations for all ordered pairs, unlike a star with zero leaf-leaf interactions and correlated reciprocal signs.
Symmetric directed valuations assure Nash existence as a special case but do not characterize nonsymmetric outcomes or the Gaussian transition.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The cited universal complexity, random dense-graph, and symmetric existence theorems neither state nor imply our all-partition count and reciprocity probability. The only directly shared consequence is existence under exact edge symmetry.

evidence: The signed-star criterion yields the full equilibrium set for any signed profile; the arbitrary-weight star hardness theorem does not specialize to a formula.
The dense random model tends to zero Nash existence under a different distribution, whereas this star model has limiting probability one above critical reciprocity.
Classical binomial reflection/central-limit and exponential formulas are employed as tools; the specific reduction of the game to sums U and R supplies their application.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither a generic hardness classification nor a continuous iid dense-graph nonexistence law determines the present signed-star exact formulas. Known symmetric-potential existence is a genuine covered subcase and is not separately claimed novel.

evidence: Hanaka–Lampis 2022: Nash stability remains strongly NP-hard on stars with unrestricted integer weights; proof uses a reduction from 3-partition with larger coefficients.
Igarashi–Elkind 2016 studies graph-restricted communication, where coalitions are graph-connected; the set of permitted outsider blocks differs from unrestricted ASHG partitions.
Bullinger 2022 analyzes consent variants and majority rules.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Other star-named results are not equivalent: arbitrary-weight hardness does not determine unit-weight equilibria; connected-coalition feasibility changes the deviation and partition spaces; consent-based stability does not coincide with unrestricted Nash stability.

originality.rationale: The mathematically closest star hardness results concern arbitrary weights, or a different connected-feasibility notion, and do not imply a binary signed-star equilibrium spectrum. Broader restricted-alphabet results concern general graphs, consent variants, or algorithmic complexity rather than this classification and random reciprocity law. The random hedonic law on dense independently valued complete graphs does not imply the sparse correlated star law. Search of recoverable prior claims and relevant literature did not identify an equivalent stronger theorem; unindexed specialist priority uncertainty remains.

value.rationale: The first exact all-instance Nash classification of a natural signed-star restriction of a known hard problem produces a full labeled equilibrium enumerator. For independent reciprocal signs, it also yields a genuine threshold at correlation 1/2, its Gaussian critical window, and an exact even/odd finite-size effect. Those are quantitative structural facts about when self-enforcing coalitions exist in a sparse central-broker system, not arbitrary parameter slices or trivial known-table recomputations.
